summary: Simulate a pen writing the characters down and up across the rows: the row index bounces between the top and the bottom (T14 — bouncing index). At the end, read the rows one after another.

blocks.title: Read the text and the row count
blocks.text: Two lines: the string stays text, the row count becomes an `int`.

blocks.title: Special case: no zigzag
blocks.text: With 1 row the bounce logic breaks: row 0 is both the top and the bottom, `step` becomes 1, and `rows[1]` crashes with `IndexError`. With at least as many rows as characters, the pen only goes straight down, so the text is unchanged.

blocks.title: One string per row, pen at the top
blocks.text: `rows` holds the text of each row. `r` is the current row and `step` is the direction (+1 down, −1 up).

blocks.title: Write the character in the current row
blocks.text: Each character goes to the row the pen is on.

blocks.title: Bounce at the edges
blocks.text: At the top row we go down; at the bottom row we go up. In between, `step` keeps its direction.

blocks.title: Move the pen and read the rows
blocks.text: `r += step` moves to the next row. After the loop, `"".join(rows)` reads the rows top to bottom.

complexity: Time O(L) with L ≤ 1000 characters — instant.
pitfalls: Changing direction one step too late, so the pen leaves the grid.
